Onomatopoeia from the flapping of a sheet of paper: ‘flimsy’ for paper, ‘fluent’ for speech that flows off the tongue.
Onomatopoeia for a dry, rattling sound → parched, bone-dry.

来 (come) + る → to come.

Clipped compound of エアコンディショナー (‘air conditioner’).

meaning: to pick up; to take away
meaning_logic: 取 (take) + 上 (above) → to take up → to pick up; to take away.

meaning: to accept something; to take in
meaning_logic: 受 (accept) + 入 (enter) → to accept and take in.

Loanword from English ‘towel’.
拭 (wipe) + く → to wipe.
柔 (tender) + らかい → soft, tender.

meaning: to get wet; to be wet

meaning_logic: 乾 (dry) + く → to get dry.
Na-adjective usually written 綺麗 — 綺 (beautiful) + 麗 (lovely) → clean, pretty.
Native word from 先 (さき) ‘ahead, previous’ with a doubled consonant → a moment ago.
急 (hurry) + ぐ → to hurry.
前 (in front) — single kanji, read まえ.
Native adverb, kana only, no standard kanji. Means slowly, at ease.
Loanword from English ‘kitchen’.

meaning: to put down; to set down
meaning_logic: 置 (put) + く → to put down.

食 (eat) + 事 (matter) → a meal.

Native verb usually written 握る — 握 (grip) + る → to grip, to hold.

家 (house) + 具 (tool) → house tools → furniture.
体 (body) — single kanji, read からだ.
お (polite prefix) + 祭 (festival) + り → a festival.
弟 (younger brother) — single kanji, read おとうと.

風 (wind) — single kanji, read かぜ.

修 (repair) + 理 (reason) → repair.

meaning_logic: 今 (now) + 朝 (morning) → this morning.
妻 (wife) — single kanji, read つま.
Native word usually written 喧嘩 — 喧 (noisy) + 嘩 (noisy) → a noisy clash → a fight, a quarrel.

病 (sick) + 院 (institution) → a hospital.
